transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what's been troubling you or what brings you in today?

Well, I came in because... I just keep feeling like I've completely let my family down, you know? Taking on this mortgage, it was... it was a big step. Too big, maybe. And every time I drop a tray or mess up an order at the restaurant—I'm a waiter, by the way, over at that Italian place on 4th Street. They make their own pasta from scratch every morning. It's actually really fascinating how they do it, they have this massive imported machine from Milan... But anyway, yeah, every small mistake I make at work just proves I'm completely useless. Like I deserve whatever bad things happen to me. I just can't shake that feeling.
How long have you been feeling this way about yourself and your performance at work?

Well, the really heavy stuff... the feeling so down and guilty all the time... that's been going on for about a year and two months. I know it's been a year and two months because it started right around the time the restaurant switched our uniform shirts. 

We used to wear these really stiff white button-downs, but then management decided to go with black polos to look more modern, I guess. They're supposed to be that moisture-wicking material, which is nice when you're running plates out to the patio in July, but they snag on absolutely everything. I caught my sleeve on the edge of the espresso machine just last week and pulled a huge thread. It's a beautiful machine, actually, a La Marzocco, but it needs to be descaled constantly because the city water here is incredibly hard. Honestly, the water quality has been getting so much worse since they changed the reservoir piping... 

But, um, wait, what did you ask me? Oh, right, how long. Yeah, so about fourteen months of just feeling awful about myself.
Have you noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in activities you used to enjoy, such as hobbies, work, or spending time with family and friends, during this time?

Yeah, I guess so. I used to be pretty social, you know? Like, I'd always joke around with the regulars at the restaurant. We have this one guy, Mr. Henderson, who comes in every Tuesday and orders the exact same thing—veal piccata, extra capers. He always brings his little dog, a pug named Barnaby, who sits in a carrier by his feet. Pugs have such terrible breathing problems, though. I read this article about how they've been bred to have those flat faces and it's actually really bad for their health. It makes you wonder about the ethics of dog breeding, honestly. Like, we're basically creating animals that are designed to suffer just because we think they look cute. It's kind of messed up when you really think about it... 

But anyway, yeah, I don't really joke with Mr. Henderson anymore. Or anyone, really. I mostly just keep a straight face and only say what I absolutely have to. And I used to text my brother all the time after my shifts, but now... I just let his messages sit there. I just don't feel any pull to answer them. It's like the energy to even type a response is just gone.
Have you noticed a decrease in your energy or found yourself feeling more fatigued than usual since you've been feeling this way?

I wouldn't say I'm more tired than usual. I mean, I'm on my feet all day at the restaurant, so I always have a baseline level of being tired after a shift, but my energy itself feels about the same. It really helps that I bought these new non-slip shoes a while back. I ordered them from this specialty workwear site, and they have these incredible memory foam insoles. 

The shipping took absolutely forever, though. I think the package was coming from a warehouse in Ohio, and there was that huge weather delay that backed up all the freight trucks across the Midwest. It's actually crazy how much we rely on the interstate system, right? Like, if one major highway shuts down, the whole supply chain just completely falls apart. You can't even get a pair of shoes on time, let alone fresh produce for the restaurant. We had to eighty-six the daily special for three days straight because the delivery truck with the heirloom tomatoes was stuck at a weigh station... 

Wait, sorry. Did you ask about my energy? Yeah, no, I haven't really noticed a decrease in my energy.
Have you felt down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, since this period of feeling awful began?

Yeah, I'd say most days. There's just this... this really heavy, empty feeling right in my chest. I just go through the motions, you know? Like, I'm carrying the plates and smiling at the tables because I'm supposed to, but... well, speaking of the plates, we actually just switched to these thick stoneware ones. Management bought them from this local pottery studio downtown. It's a nice idea, supporting local businesses and all, but they are ridiculously heavy to carry on a tray. And they chip if you even look at them wrong. 

Our dishwasher, Hector, gets so incredibly stressed out about it because they blame him if they break. He's this really great guy, he's been trying to save up for a down payment on a house for his family, but the housing market right now is just completely broken. I mean, with the interest rates doing what they're doing, how is a normal person supposed to afford anything? It's like the whole system is rigged against the working class, you know? The banks just keep raising rates and... 

But, um... sorry, I'm doing it again. To answer your question, yeah. I just smile at work because it's my job, not because I actually feel anything good anymore. It's pretty much every day.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight over the past year and two months?

Yeah, my eating has been pretty all over the place, honestly. Like, some weeks I barely even touch the staff meal before my shift. We usually get whatever the kitchen is trying to get rid of, which is fine, but... well, last week they made this massive batch of chicken cacciatore because the supplier sent us three extra cases of bell peppers by mistake. The peppers were actually really good, they were those bright yellow and red ones, not the cheap green ones that taste bitter. 

It's weird how much the color of a vegetable can change the flavor, right? Like, I read that red bell peppers are just green ones that have been left on the vine longer, so they have more time to develop sugars and vitamins. It makes you wonder why green ones are so much cheaper at the grocery store if they're literally the exact same plant. I guess time is money in farming, just like everywhere else. The agriculture industry is wild when you look into it, especially with all the subsidies for corn and soy, but barely anything for specialty crops...

Oh, but right, my appetite. So yeah, some weeks I don't eat at work at all. But then other nights, I'll come home after my shift and just eat whatever's in the kitchen. I'll just stand there in front of the fridge and eat just to feel... I don't know, settled, I guess. So it's been really up and down.
Have you felt excessive guilt or believed that you are worthless more days than not during this period?

Yeah, I... I do. A lot, actually. I just keep feeling like I've completely let my family down by taking on this mortgage. It's like this constant weight. And then every small mistake I make at work, like if I forget a side of ranch or punch in the wrong table number, it just proves to me that I'm completely useless and I deserve whatever bad things happen to me. 

Speaking of the point of sale system at work, they just updated the software last month, and it is a complete disaster. The interface used to be color-coded by course—appetizers were blue, mains were green—but now everything is just this uniform gray block of text. It's so hard to read in the dim lighting of the dining room. I don't understand why tech companies feel the need to constantly update things that are already working perfectly fine. It's like they just have to justify their own existence by changing the UI every six months. My brother-in-law works in software development, actually. He does front-end stuff for a medical billing company, and he says half the time they're just moving buttons around to make it look fresh for the investors. It's all about optics, right? Nobody actually cares about the end user who has to stare at the screen for eight hours a day. He gets paid an absolute fortune to do it, too. Makes you wonder about the value of labor, honestly... 

But, uh, yeah. Sorry. The guilt. Yes, I feel like I'm worthless most days. It's really hard to shake.
Have you noticed yourself moving or speaking more slowly than usual, or on the contrary, feeling restless and unable to sit still?

Yeah, actually... people at work have been pointing it out. Like, sometimes I get so restless I just pace around the dining room, checking the same tables and double-checking receipts over and over. It's like I can't stop moving. But then other times, I get so slowed down that just grabbing menus and walking over to the POS system takes me way longer than it should. It's like moving through molasses. 

Which, by the way, we actually use real molasses in our barbecue sauce at the restaurant. The chef insists on it. He says it gives it this authentic Southern depth that you just can't get with brown sugar or corn syrup. We buy it in these massive five-gallon buckets, and it is incredibly sticky. If you spill even a drop of it in the prep area, it's like a magnet for fruit flies. We had this huge fruit fly infestation last summer because someone didn't seal the bucket right. The exterminator told us that fruit flies can lay up to 500 eggs at a time, which is just horrifying if you think about it. They breed in drains, mostly. We had to pour boiling water and bleach down every sink in the kitchen for a week straight just to get rid of them. It's crazy how resilient bugs are. Like, cockroaches can survive nuclear fallout, right? I read somewhere that insects will probably outlive humanity because they just adapt so fast to whatever environment they're in...

But, um, what were we talking about? Oh, the moving slow and fast thing. Yeah, my coworkers definitely notice it. I'm either bouncing off the walls or dragging my feet.
